figures.finding: A child is a person under eighteen, and the Child's Rights Act speaks of majority as the end of childhood, so majority is eighteen where the Act is in force.
figures.applies: Federal Act (in force in the Federal Capital Territory and in each state that has enacted it; the states' enactments were not traced).

sources.said: "child" means, a person under the age of eighteen years; ... no action shall be brought against a child by a person after the child has attained the age of majority, to pay a debt contracted before majority

figures.finding: The two Acts govern different things and stack. The Labour Act, in force everywhere, defines a child as under twelve and a young person as under eighteen: no one under twelve may work save light agricultural, horticultural or domestic work for his family approved by the Minister; from twelve a young person may work, but under fourteen only by the day and returning home each night, under fifteen not in an industrial undertaking, under sixteen not away from home without a labour officer's approval and a written contract, not more than four hours at a stretch or eight a day, and not at night (10 p.m. to 6 a.m.). The Child's Rights Act, in the Federal Capital Territory and each state that has enacted it, defines a child as under eighteen and forbids employing a child in any capacity save the same family light work, and in any industrial undertaking; and it applies the Labour Act's young-person sections 58 to 63 to every child. So where the Child's Rights Act is in force the working age is eighteen, with family light work the only exception and the Labour Act's hours, night and contract rules governing it; where it is not, twelve, with those rules. Neither Act makes an exception for acting or other performing work.

figures.applies: Labour Act nationwide; Child's Rights Act in the FCT and the states that have enacted it (the Federal Ministry of Information says all 36 had by November 2024; other counts differ, see majority).

sources.said: (1) No child shall- (a) be employed or work in any capacity except where he is employed by a mem- ber of his fantily on light work of an agricultural, horticultural or domestic character approved by the Minister; … (2) No young person under the age of fifteen years shall be employed or work in any industrial undertaking: … (3) A young person under the age of fourteen years may be employed only- (a) on a daily wage; (b) on a day-to-day basis; and … (8) No young person under the age of sixteen years shall be required to work for a longer period than four consecutive hours or permitted to work for more than eight working hours in one day:

(a) in the case of young persons under the age of sixteen years, the interval be- tween ten o'clock in the evening and six o'clock in the morning; … "child" means a young person under the age oftwelve years; … "young person" means a person under the age of eighteen years.

(1) Subject to this Act, no child shall be‐ (a) subjected to any forced or exploitative labour; or (b) employed to work in any capacity except where he is employed by a member of his family on light work of an agricultural, horticultural or domestic character; or … (2) No child shall be employed or work in an industrial undertaking … The provisions relating to young persons in sections 58, 59, 60, 61, 62 and 63 of the Labour Act shall apply to children under this Act. … "child" means, a person under the age of eighteen years;

figures.finding: A child may contract only as the Child's Rights Act allows: loans and goods other than necessaries are void and cannot be enforced after majority; under the Labour Act a young person under sixteen working away from home needs a labour officer's approval and a written contract, which then can't be voided for infancy; no rule setting aside earnings or naming creative work was found.

value.binding: Child's Rights Act s. 18; for under-16s working away from home, an authorised labour officer's approval and a written contract (Labour Act s. 59(4))

figures.applies: Federal; Child's Rights Act where in force.

sources.said: 18. Contractual rights of a child (1) No child shall enter into a contract, except as provided in this section. (2) Any contract, except a contact for necessaries, entered into by a child for repayment of money lent or for payment of goods supplied to the child, shall be void.

(4) No young person under the age of sixteen years shall be employed in circum- stances in which it is not reasonably possible for him to return each day to the place of residence of his parent or guardian except- (a) with the approval of an authorised labour officer; and (b) on a written contract (which, notwithstanding any law to the contrary, shall not be voidable on the ground of incapacity to contract due to infancy)

figures.finding: The Bank of Industry's Nollyfund lends only to companies engaged in film production, so a person applies through his company (see companies).
figures.applies: As the Bank of Industry describes the fund, read 2026-11-01.

sources.said: The Fund can be accessed by Companies engaged in film production.

figures.finding: No one under eighteen may join in forming a company unless two others not disqualified also subscribe, a minor isn't counted toward the minimum membership, and no one under eighteen may be a director.
figures.applies: Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020, in force 2021.

sources.said: 20.—(1) Subject to subsection (2), an individual shall not join in the formation of a company under this Act if he is— (a) less than 18 years of age ; ... (2) A person shall not be disqualified under subsection (1) (a), if two other persons not disqualified under that subsection have subscribed to the memorandum. ... (2) A person under the age of 18 years shall not be counted for the purpose of determining the legal minimum number of members of a company. ... 283. The following persons shall be disqualified from being director— (a) an infant, that is, a person under the age of 18 years ;

figures.finding: The Federal Ministry of Information stated in November 2024 that all 36 states have adopted the Child's Rights Act, so majority at eighteen reaches the whole federation by that account; earlier ministers' and UNICEF's counts (24, 25, 31 states) differ and no state-by-state list was found.
figures.applies: As the Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation stated it for Universal Children's Day 2024.
